main_body: Thatched hip roof (rows 5-54) over a log-plank front wall with a central doorway (rows 55-78)
top_band: Thatch roof slope, rows 7-54, tan/gold L=124-154 with dark course lines every 5 rows, seen from above and foreshortened. The step to the front wall is at the eave, rows ~54-56
evidence: The roof is a large sloped surface that fills the upper two thirds. Its side edges step outward toward the eave, so it reads as a hipped roof seen from above, like the reference house roofs. The lighter eave course at the bottom of the thatch is the front edge, and a dark row under it shades the log wall. The door has a timber frame, a stone sill and a dark interior, so it is inset. The round shields and plank grain add wall detail. The column scan shows no separate light cap, but for a building the roof slope is the top surface, so this is not a front elevation.

style.evidence: The thatch uses about 4 tones with a per-course highlight and dark line, and the wood uses about 4 browns with plank grain and shield detail. The outline is dark brown, tinted to match the neighbouring material, and only 13% of dark edge pixels are neutral. Flat-fill coverage is 2%. The median of 9 colours per tile is close to house-h112 (11) and below house-h101 (18). The total of 38 colours is lower than both references. The thatch courses repeat mechanically, which is a little thinner than the reference tile roofs, but nothing reads as a flat sticker.
